candidate.text: show your mettle, then, and make yourself a name in story.

candidate.context: Athena tells Telemachus he is old enough to act and win a name.

candidate.text: One day, the oar would be mistaken for a winnowing shovel.
candidate.basis: Tiresias's inland-oar prophecy gives the object a new meaning far from the sea.
candidate.fit: Source-led interpretation of the future shrine rather than a literal amulet.

candidate.text: A house survives an absence by turning every new duty into another day endured.
candidate.basis: Book II supplies the household under prolonged pressure; the three-step enchantment progression is a deliberate composite.
candidate.fit: Turns the household-composite making brief into usable flavour without falsely quoting one character.

candidate.text: I will begin by disguising you so that no human being shall know you

candidate.speaker: Athena
candidate.context: Athena tells Odysseus she will alter him beyond recognition before he enters his own household.
candidate.fit: This is the exact action behind the intervention/appearance reset.

candidate.text: The crew survived by refusing the song they could not afford to hear.
candidate.basis: The crew stops its ears and rows while Odysseus listens bound to the mast.
candidate.fit: Centers collective discipline rather than Odysseus's exceptional access.

candidate.text: no one ever yet came who was so like Ulysses in figure, voice, and feet as you are

candidate.fit: The line makes washing a recognition scene before the decisive physical proof.

cards.name: Seat the Guest by the Hearth

candidate.text: He had waited twenty years for one last certainty.
candidate.basis: Argos recognises Odysseus immediately and dies only after seeing him home.
candidate.fit: Avoids repeating the exact wagged-tail quotation already attached to this vertical.

candidate.text: it is I, as you will shortly learn, who have convened you

candidate.location: Book 2, Telemachus opens the assembly
candidate.speaker: Telemachus
candidate.context: Telemachus publicly claims responsibility for calling the first assembly since Odysseus left.

candidate.context: Calypso tells Odysseus to keep the Bear on his left while navigating.

candidate.text: The sea had waited for Poseidon to notice him.

candidate.text: A good singer chooses the story. A great one discovers what the listener cannot hide.
candidate.basis: Book VIII repeatedly shows song selecting, shaping and exposing emotional memory.
candidate.fit: An original line for an ordinary bard without stealing Demodocus's specific quotations.

candidate.text: Knowledge became safe only after temptation had spent itself against the ropes.
candidate.basis: Odysseus can hear the Sirens only because restraint was arranged in advance.
candidate.fit: Turns the Ordeal's repeated Survival checks into precommitted resistance.

candidate.text: Every road not taken left a mark on the one that remained.
candidate.basis: Odysseus repeatedly chooses among dangerous courses and uncertain divine advice.
candidate.fit: Source-led interpretation for the set's exile/face-up journey mechanic.

candidate.text: lay him down upon the sand still fast asleep
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 13, the Phaeacians deliver Odysseus home

candidate.context: The Phaeacians carry the sleeping Odysseus from the ship and leave him safely on Ithaca.
candidate.fit: A precise homecoming that feels like arrival without immediate awareness.

candidate.text: The perfect lie saved him. The truth nearly undid it.
candidate.basis: Nobody defeats the Cyclops's call for help; Odysseus later boasts his true name and enables the curse.
candidate.fit: The emotional hinge is pride after successful cunning.

candidate.text: Freedom began as timber, measured and cut by hand.
candidate.basis: Odysseus personally selects, cuts, smooths and joins the timber for his raft.
candidate.fit: Keeps the emphasis on earned agency rather than miraculous rescue.

candidate.text: The voyage could continue only after the dead were given their due.
candidate.basis: Elpenor's burial shows funeral labour interrupting the voyage until obligation is completed.
candidate.fit: Generalises direct funeral work into an anonymous attendant.

candidate.text: if I am to be eaten out of house and home at all
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 2, Telemachus condemns the suitors' consumption
candidate.speaker: Telemachus
candidate.context: Telemachus describes the suitors consuming his estate without recourse.

candidate.text: Even the least glorious companion could not be left without a name and grave.

candidate.fit: Frames funeral duty as obligation rather than heroic reward.

candidate.text: The blood did not raise the dead. It gave them permission to speak.
candidate.basis: The trench, blood and controlled access let particular shades answer Odysseus.
candidate.fit: Distinguishes consultation from broad resurrection.

candidate.text: Now, stranger, I shall put you to the test
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 19, Penelope tests the beggar's story
candidate.speaker: Penelope
candidate.context: Penelope asks for remembered details of Odysseus's clothing and companions.

candidate.fit: Gift/hospitality without requiring recognition.

candidate.text: Each crossing taught the crew what the next storm would demand.
candidate.basis: Book V treats sea travel as repeated endurance and adaptation; this card generalises that voyage pattern.
candidate.fit: Composite voyage flavour rather than a claim of one specific gale-rowing scene.

candidate.text: The embassy became a meal before anyone understood the welcome.

candidate.fit: Captures Laestrygonian hospitality as predation.

candidate.text: Tell me, O muse

candidate.location: Book 1, opening invocation
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: The singer invokes divine assistance to tell the journey.

candidate.context: The scar is felt during the foot-washing; Eurycleia's recognition physically upsets the basin.
candidate.fit: The artifact is the setting where hidden identity becomes undeniable.

candidate.text: Before a ship can brave the sea, someone must master fire beside it.

candidate.fit: Explicit material-world extension.

candidate.text: The feast continued after the prophet had already seen its ending.
candidate.basis: Theoclymenus sees blood, ghosts and darkness while the suitors laugh at him.

candidate.text: The tool that shaped the raft made every later mile possible.
candidate.basis: Calypso gives Odysseus an adze, which he uses in the raft construction.
candidate.fit: Source-led object flavour without quoting another Book V line.

candidate.text: The story was false. The kindness it tested was not.
candidate.basis: Odysseus tells the cold-night cloak story to see whether Eumaeus will care for him; Eumaeus supplies cloak and bedding.
candidate.fit: The card is about testing character through an invented story.

candidate.text: Every landing was a question disguised as land.
candidate.basis: Books IX–XII repeatedly turn new shores into uncertain tests of people, food and danger.
candidate.fit: Whole-voyage composite for exploration/ramp.

candidate.text: Songs survive because memory changes them just enough to sing again.

candidate.text: When one man's strength failed, rhythm carried the ship.
candidate.basis: Odysseus repeatedly orders coordinated rowing through danger.
candidate.fit: Original crew-work line grounded in the passage.

candidate.text: The horizon vanished before the sailor had time to name the weather.
candidate.basis: Poseidon's storm rapidly covers earth, sea and sky with cloud.

candidate.text: The disguise hid the king; it could not hide the servant's character.

candidate.fit: Moral test rather than literal magical debuff.

candidate.text: He survived by holding still above a danger that never did.

candidate.text: A house stands because something bears its weight.

candidate.text: The god gave him a flower, a warning, and exactly enough courage to enter.
candidate.basis: Hermes gives moly and instructions before Odysseus confronts Circe.
candidate.fit: Practical divine intervention rather than automatic victory.

candidate.text: I will find you a ship, and will come with you myself.

candidate.speaker: Athena in Mentor's likeness

candidate.author: Homer

candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 20, Theoclymenus's vision
candidate.speaker: Theoclymenus
candidate.context: The prophet sees blood, ghosts and darkness over the hall and announces the suitors' doom.
candidate.fit: A compact image from the exact vision gives the black Omen dread without explaining the whole prophecy.

candidate.text: The flame marked the place where obligation became memory.
candidate.basis: Elpenor's body and armour are burned before cairn and oar memorial are raised.
candidate.fit: Direct funeral image generalised into the card.

candidate.text: One voice kept time so many hands could become one motion.
candidate.basis: Coordinated rowing is textual; a formal rowing chant is a historical seamanship extension.
candidate.fit: Rhythm rather than a claimed Homeric song.

candidate.text: The crew trusted the sailor who knew when motion should become patience.
candidate.basis: The voyage repeatedly alternates action with waiting for usable conditions.
candidate.fit: Original weatherwise-sailor composite.

candidate.text: The cliffs became weapons as soon as the harbor became a trap.
candidate.basis: Laestrygonians hurl rocks down onto ships trapped inside the landlocked harbour.
candidate.fit: Direct environmental violence.

candidate.text: Poseidon broke in moments what patience had built in days.
candidate.basis: The storm smashes the raft Odysseus had spent days constructing.
candidate.fit: The Elemental is a game personification of the destructive sea.

candidate.text: the joints upon the spits began to low like cows
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 12, omen after Helios's cattle are slaughtered
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: After the crew violates the taboo, the hides crawl and the roasting meat bellows before punishment follows.
candidate.fit: The uncanny physical sign is the card's exact image and carries the horror of the violated oath.

candidate.text: A long voyage learns to make tomorrow's food out of today's catch.
candidate.basis: Preserved fish is an ancient-Mediterranean food extension rather than a named Odyssey meal.
candidate.fit: Material-world travel flavour.

candidate.text: On the empty island, abundance waited for people who had not earned it.
candidate.basis: The goat-rich island opposite the Cyclopes is untouched by farming or hunters.
candidate.fit: Natural-world composite.

candidate.text: there will be no house in Ithaca more royal than your own
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 15, Theoclymenus interprets the hawk
candidate.speaker: Theoclymenus
candidate.context: A hawk carrying a dove crosses on the right and is read as a sign of the enduring rule of Odysseus's house.
candidate.fit: It states the interpretation of the bird omen rather than merely describing the animal.

candidate.text: The goats had the island to themselves until hungry sailors arrived.
candidate.basis: Odysseus's crew hunts the abundant wild goats on the uninhabited island.
candidate.fit: Direct scene with ordinary fauna.

candidate.text: The dead gathered where blood and promise met.
candidate.basis: Libation, sacrifice and vows draw the shades to the trench.
candidate.fit: Ritual contact rather than generic resurrection.

candidate.text: The passenger slept because everyone else agreed to carry the danger for him.
candidate.basis: The Phaeacians escort Odysseus home asleep, handling ship, gifts and landing collectively.
candidate.fit: Protective Vehicle flavour rather than supernatural speed.

candidate.text: the child of morning, rosy-fingered Dawn, appeared
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 2, recurring dawn formula
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: The repeated formula marks a new day and renewed action.
candidate.fit: The exact formula is the card's identity.

candidate.text: the man is guiltless, do him no hurt
candidate.location: Book 22, Telemachus defends Medon
candidate.speaker: Telemachus
candidate.context: Telemachus intervenes so the innocent herald Medon is spared.
candidate.fit: The line exactly captures Medon's survival amid the household deaths.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: Hospitality begins by raising the stranger from the ashes.
candidate.basis: Alcinous raises the suppliant from the hearth before seating him.
candidate.fit: Source-led adaptation distinct from the exact quote used on Seat the Guest.

candidate.text: Their ships seemed to know the destination before the sailors spoke it.
candidate.basis: Alcinous says Phaeacian ships understand their passengers' intended destination.
candidate.fit: The shipwright is invented; the impossible craft is directly Homeric.

candidate.text: change your song and tell us of the wooden horse
candidate.location: Book 8, Odysseus requests Demodocus's Trojan Horse song
candidate.speaker: Odysseus
candidate.context: Odysseus asks Demodocus to sing the story of the wooden horse.
candidate.fit: It makes the card's status as an actual performed song explicit.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: Knowing the monster was coming did not make it a fight he could win.
candidate.basis: Circe warns that Scylla is invincible and instructs Odysseus to pass quickly.
candidate.fit: Foreknowledge without mastery.

candidate.text: His crew obeyed him best by refusing his orders.
candidate.basis: Odysseus orders the crew to bind him tighter if he begs to be released.
candidate.fit: A paradox of trust and restraint.

candidate.text: so long shall we go on eating up your estate
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 2, Antinous defends the suitors' consumption
candidate.speaker: Antinous
candidate.context: Antinous openly states that the suitors will continue consuming Telemachus's estate.
candidate.fit: The line turns hunger into deliberate predation rather than abstract scarcity.

candidate.text: I will bring you arms from the store room
candidate.location: Book 22, Melanthius arms the suitors
candidate.speaker: Melanthius
candidate.context: Melanthius volunteers to fetch weapons for the suitors during the hall battle.
candidate.fit: A direct statement of his active betrayal and resource conversion.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: A house expecting violence can make every threshold feel haunted.
candidate.basis: Book XX concentrates dread, divine signs and visions of ghosts; the specific Nightmare creature is an extension.
candidate.fit: Explicit dream/threshold extension rather than a claimed monster episode.

candidate.text: he could stir or still each one of them according to his own pleasure
candidate.location: Book 10, Aeolus controls the winds
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: Aeolus is described as able to rouse or quiet the winds at will.
candidate.fit: The line maps directly onto his Vehicle acceleration and wind-bottling Adventure.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: On a bare coast, weather has nowhere to hide its violence.
candidate.basis: Odysseus's landfall is exposed to storm, surf and rock.
candidate.fit: Landscape extension rather than a distinct named storm.

candidate.text: Every gift they mistrusted and every warning they ignored became another verse.
candidate.basis: The wind bag and later cattle episode form a composite cautionary pattern.
candidate.fit: Imagined song explicitly marked as composite.

candidate.text: A useful thing often begins with discarding the failed one.
candidate.basis: Book V supplies intensive practical making; the iterative bench-work engine is an extension.
candidate.fit: Original craft-process flavour.

candidate.text: The cave taught them that escape could be quieter than victory.
candidate.basis: The surviving crew escapes under sheep rather than defeating Polyphemus outright.
candidate.fit: Endurance and stealth over conquest.

candidate.text: He looked like some lion of the wilderness
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 6, Odysseus emerges before Nausicaa
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: The naked, salt-caked Odysseus is compared to a famished lion as the maids scatter.
candidate.fit: The card is the simile itself, so the direct line is preferable to an adaptation.

candidate.text: watching the seals come up in hundreds to bask upon the sea shore
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 4, Menelaus waits for Proteus
candidate.speaker: Menelaus
candidate.context: Menelaus describes waiting among the seals during the Proteus episode.
candidate.fit: The card is a setting/fauna treatment and must stay attached to Menelaus's story, not Odysseus's.

candidate.text: let us call her and see whether she is woman or goddess.
candidate.location: Book 10, Polites urges the crew toward Circe's house
candidate.speaker: Polites
candidate.context: Polites persuades the scouting party to call to the singer inside Circe's house.
candidate.fit: It captures the decisive first-through-the-door impulse behind the card.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: at night I would unpick the stitches
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 19, Penelope recounts the shroud deception
candidate.speaker: Penelope
candidate.context: She explains to the disguised Odysseus how she postponed the marriage.
candidate.fit: The action is exactly the rare proposal's unweaving hook.

candidate.text: when they had drunk she turned them into pigs by a stroke of her wand
candidate.location: Book 10, Circe transforms the crew
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: Circe drugs and transforms Odysseus's companions.
candidate.fit: The exact transformation scene grounds the face-down/enchantment-death identity.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: you would stay where you are, keep house along with me
candidate.location: Book 5, Calypso urges Odysseus to remain
candidate.speaker: Calypso
candidate.context: Calypso offers continued life with her on Ogygia instead of departure.
candidate.fit: The line directly expresses comfort becoming captivity and delayed homecoming.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: Father, I have always heard of your renown both in the field and in council
candidate.location: Book 16, Telemachus recognises Odysseus
candidate.speaker: Telemachus
candidate.context: After the reunion, Telemachus addresses the father whose reputation he has inherited.
candidate.fit: It bridges returned son, inherited identity, and the coming coordinated fight.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: if anything has been said amiss may the winds blow it away with them
candidate.location: Book 8, Euryalus apologises to Odysseus
candidate.speaker: Euryalus
candidate.context: After insulting Odysseus and seeing his athletic prowess, Euryalus apologises and offers a gift.
candidate.fit: It completes Euryalus's sequence from challenge to recognition and reconciliation.
candidate.author: Homer

candidate.text: The dead remain part of a house as long as someone still tends their memory.
candidate.basis: Book XXIV supplies named ghosts and family memory; the ordinary grave-keeper remains a funerary/social-world composite.
candidate.fit: Gives the composite a source-led line without inventing a literal grave-tending scene.

candidate.text: No sea was wide enough to delay the messenger of Zeus.
candidate.basis: Hermes crosses land and sea in divine sandals to deliver Zeus's order.
candidate.fit: Specific to Hermes while remaining an adaptation of the narration.

candidate.text: The hall glowed because secrecy itself had divine help.
candidate.basis: Athena carries a golden lamp while Odysseus and Telemachus remove the armour.
candidate.fit: Distinguishes supernatural illumination from the ordinary oil lamp.

candidate.text: my mother does not know anything about it
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 2, Telemachus secretly loads the ship
candidate.speaker: Telemachus
candidate.context: Telemachus tells the crew that Penelope does not know about the stores or departure.
candidate.fit: A concise expression of the secret voyage.

candidate.text: Speed is another kind of shelter when the sea turns hostile.
candidate.basis: Ordinary fast-galley play is a seamanship extension distinct from supernatural Phaeacian ships.
candidate.fit: Original extension for evasive Vehicle play.

candidate.text: settled them in Scheria, far from all other people
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 6, the Phaeacians' settlement
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: Nausithous establishes the Phaeacians in remote Scheria.
candidate.fit: Directly supports the renamed Uncharted Haven treatment.

candidate.text: Every ship entered the passage knowing someone might not leave it.
candidate.basis: Circe says no ship passes Scylla without losing men.
candidate.fit: Setting as unavoidable cost.

candidate.text: On Aeaea, welcome and transformation arrived in the same cup.
candidate.basis: Circe's house combines hospitality, food and transforming drugs.
candidate.fit: Place flavour for seductive danger.

candidate.text: The stone in the doorway mattered more than any weapon inside.
candidate.basis: Polyphemus's immense door-stone makes killing him immediately impossible.
candidate.fit: The cave itself is the prison.

candidate.text: Beauty and danger grew from the same enchanted ground.
candidate.basis: Aeaea is Circe's dangerous domain; 'garden' is a treatment, not a named Book XI setting.
candidate.fit: Corrects the old Book XI source drift.

candidate.text: let us rather set about stowing your things at once in the cave
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 13, Athena secures the Phaeacian gifts
candidate.speaker: Athena
candidate.context: Athena directs Odysseus to hide his treasures in the cave of the Naiads.
candidate.fit: The cave's gameplay identity is security and preserved future value.

candidate.text: She changed bodies before she changed minds.
candidate.basis: Circe's draught and wand transform the crew while the story remains about identity and control.
candidate.fit: Mythic portrayal centred on transformation power.

candidate.text: Immortality was only another name for never leaving.
candidate.basis: Calypso offers immortality if Odysseus remains, while he longs for home.
candidate.fit: Separates the mythic shelter fantasy from a freely chosen happy ending.

candidate.text: a thoroughly good woman both in head and heart
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 7, Athena describes Arete
candidate.speaker: Athena
candidate.context: Athena tells Odysseus that Arete's judgement can secure his homeward passage.
candidate.fit: A concise portrait of Arete's respected discernment.

candidate.text: The sea forgets no crossing; sailors do.
candidate.basis: The whole voyage accumulates remembered routes and losses; the sea-memory premise is an original metaphor.
candidate.fit: Odyssey-wide rather than one episode.

candidate.text: What the sea lost to her returned only when she chose.
candidate.basis: Charybdis cyclically swallows and disgorges the sea.
candidate.fit: Monster identity as recurrence.

candidate.text: Six mouths made choice irrelevant.
candidate.basis: Scylla strikes simultaneously with six heads and takes six sailors.
candidate.fit: Abrupt predation, not a fair combat.

candidate.text: Nothing on Thrinacia escaped the sight of the Sun.
candidate.basis: Helios's sacred cattle are protected by divine awareness and vengeance.
candidate.fit: All-seeing ownership and taboo.

candidate.text: He went to the dead because the living had run out of answers.
candidate.basis: Odysseus crosses to the shades specifically to obtain Tiresias's guidance.
candidate.fit: Journey as desperate consultation.

candidate.text: Every thread carried the patience of a household built to last.
candidate.basis: Book VII explicitly praises Phaeacian weaving; dyeing is an invented textile extension.
candidate.fit: Original flavour avoids inventing a named dyer.

candidate.text: Hunger made the warning sound negotiable.
candidate.basis: The starving crew knowingly slaughters Helios's cattle despite repeated warnings.
candidate.fit: Temptation becomes collective rationalisation.

candidate.text: They forgot home before they forgot their own names.
candidate.basis: Lotus-eaters remove the desire to return, not identity by violence.
candidate.fit: Comfort as loss of purpose.

candidate.text: The song offered wisdom at the price of ever leaving.
candidate.basis: The Sirens promise knowledge while the bones around them reveal the true cost.
candidate.fit: Knowledge as lethal compulsion.

candidate.text: The smallest life in Ithaca kept moving beneath histories too large to notice it.
candidate.basis: The hare is Mediterranean natural-world texture, not a narrated Book XIX animal.
candidate.fit: Deliberately quiet environmental flavour.

cards.name: The Siege of Troy // The Wooden Horse

candidate.text: the city was doomed when it took in that horse
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 8, Demodocus sings the wooden horse
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: Demodocus recounts the Trojan decision to bring the wooden horse into the city.
candidate.fit: Exact fatal hinge for the Saga-to-Vehicle transformation.

candidate.text: A king among the dead still spoke first of betrayal at home.
candidate.basis: Agamemnon's shade narrates his murder and warns Odysseus about homecoming.
candidate.fit: Bitterness turned into counsel.

candidate.text: Grief gave the dead shape long enough to be remembered.
candidate.basis: The blood-trench scene temporarily gives shades voice and identity; the lament is invented.
candidate.fit: Adaptive lament grounded in ritual.

candidate.text: Punishment became landscape around Tityus.
candidate.basis: Odysseus sees Tityus stretched out under endless avian punishment.
candidate.fit: Visual analogy for the reprint treatment.

candidate.text: The king answered a question by eating the messenger.
candidate.basis: Antiphates kills and eats one scout before the Laestrygonian attack begins.
candidate.fit: Predatory kingship in one action.

candidate.text: They opened the bag for gold and found distance instead.
candidate.basis: The crew mistakes Aeolus's sealed winds for hidden wealth and loses the almost-completed voyage.
candidate.fit: Temptation, force and lost progress.

candidate.text: Six cries were gone before the oars could change rhythm.
candidate.basis: Scylla takes six sailors at once during the passage.
candidate.fit: Abrupt loss that the crew cannot meaningfully answer.

candidate.text: A deed ends. The song decides how long it lives.
candidate.basis: Book VIII repeatedly turns heroic action into performed memory and future song.
candidate.fit: Original articulation of kleos through performance.

candidate.text: Aeolus gave them the wind; envy decided when it would be released.
candidate.basis: Aeolus carefully seals the winds; the crew opens the bag near home.
candidate.fit: Control undone by mistrust.

candidate.text: Helios did not need to strike them himself; he only needed Zeus to listen.
candidate.basis: Helios demands punishment after the cattle are killed; Zeus destroys the ship.
candidate.fit: Retribution through divine hierarchy.

candidate.text: Seven years can feel like one long afternoon when nothing is allowed to change.
candidate.basis: Odysseus recounts seven years on Ogygia; literal time distortion is not in Homer.
candidate.fit: Makes the time metaphor explicit without claiming time travel.

candidate.text: Every headland looked survivable from far enough away.
candidate.basis: Rocky coasts and dangerous approaches recur throughout the wanderings; this land is a composite.
candidate.fit: Landscape danger without false localization.

candidate.text: Every exposed shore taught the wind a different voice.
candidate.basis: Book V is saturated with shifting wind and exposed sea travel; the named isle is invented.
candidate.fit: Landscape-composite flavour.

candidate.text: Pride entered the games before any athlete did.
candidate.basis: The Phaeacian games turn hospitality into competition, insult and restitution.
candidate.fit: Original line for a later-laurel visual shorthand.

candidate.text: A strange shore can resemble home for exactly as long as the shade lasts.
candidate.basis: The palm imagery comes from Odysseus's speech to Nausicaa; Palmshade Cove itself is invented.
candidate.fit: Source-led landscape interpretation without relocating the Delos palm literally.

candidate.text: it was she, not he, that would have it so
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 5, Odysseus's life with Calypso
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: The narration distinguishes Calypso's desire from Odysseus's unwilling captivity.
candidate.fit: Essential corrective against romanticising this portrayal as freely chosen refuge.

candidate.text: The staff made the king look harmless long enough to learn who was not.
candidate.basis: The staff completes the beggar appearance while Odysseus enters, begs and judges the suitors.
candidate.fit: Prop as reconnaissance rather than heroic weapon.

candidate.text: he mixed them a bowl of sweet wine
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 3, Nestor hosts Telemachus
candidate.speaker: Narrator
candidate.context: Nestor mixes a bowl of aged wine for the household gathering.
candidate.fit: Specific material-world flavour distinct from the common service action.

candidate.text: The dead gave knowledge only to those willing to carry it back.
candidate.basis: The Hades journey is valuable because Odysseus returns with prophecy, obligation and memory.
candidate.fit: Ordeal as listening and return.

candidate.text: No estate can stand such recklessness
candidate.author: Homer
candidate.location: Book 2, Telemachus on the suitors' banquets
candidate.speaker: Telemachus
candidate.context: Telemachus says the constant banquets will ruin the household.
candidate.fit: A clean summary of depleted stores without duplicating Suitor's Extortion's wording.

candidate.text: The narrow sea offered no safe choice, only a survivable one.
candidate.basis: Circe explicitly frames the passage as a choice between dangers, with Scylla the lesser loss.
candidate.fit: Acceptance of necessary danger.

candidate.text: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.
candidate.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
candidate.location: Final line
candidate.speaker: Tennyson's Ulysses
candidate.context: The later poem ends with resolve to continue voyaging.
candidate.fit: Matches the deliberately restless reception version rather than Homeric homecoming.

candidate.text: Absence tests an oath by removing every immediate reward for keeping it.
candidate.basis: Eumaeus remains devoted to Odysseus despite years without proof of return or personal gain.
candidate.fit: Oath interpretation grounded in loyalty rather than a literal formal oath scene.

candidate.text: The best course is the one the sea has already begun to reveal.

candidate.text: A crew becomes one body only after every hand accepts the rhythm.

candidate.text: The shore beyond sight was already shaping the voyage before anyone could name it.

candidate.context: Autolycus is explicitly characterised by exceptional theft and false oaths.

candidate.text: we can both of us deceive upon occasion

candidate.location: Book 13, Athena recognises Odysseus's kindred cunning
candidate.speaker: Athena
